key_insight: EvolveNav turns zero-shot object-goal navigation into a self-improving process: the agent can reflect on its mistakes, extract useful navigation rules, and update its memory during test time. This reduces repeated errors and makes foundation-model-based navigation more adaptive in new environments.
problem_solved: The paper addresses zero-shot object-goal navigation, where embodied agents must find a target object without task-specific training. Existing foundation-model-based methods often rely on static priors, so they fail to adapt and keep making the same mistakes during exploration.
method: Proactive preflection: the agent anticipates likely failures and reflects before making navigation decisions.
Self-evolving memory: it extracts actionable rules from experience and continuously updates its rule memory at test time.
Closed-loop improvement: the system uses past outcomes to refine future exploration and reduce repeated trial-and-error behavior.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical path toward more adaptive embodied agents that improve without retraining. It is especially useful for zero-shot robotics and navigation settings where environments change and static policies are not enough.

paper_title: EvolveNav: Proactive Preflection and Self-Evolving Memory for Zero-Shot Object Goal Navigation
paper_authors: Qi Chai, Wenhao Shen, Nanjie Yao, Yue Xia, Kaiyong Zhao
